rules.title: Prohibition of discrimination based on a tenant's source of income (including housing vouchers and rental assistance)
rules.requirement: A San Diego landlord may not refuse to rent or renew, end a tenancy, falsely say a unit is unavailable, or advertise a preference based on your source of income, which includes Section 8 and other rental, deposit, or homeless assistance. Any income standard must count all of your income, including assistance, plus the combined income of co-tenants and cosigners.
rules.key_value: Damages of 3x one month's rent per violation

coverage.summary: All rental units in the City of San Diego, except tenancies where the owner or a family member lives in the same building and shares a bathroom or kitchen with the tenant.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Owner or owner's family member lives in the same building and shares a bathroom or kitchen with the tenant

rules.exemptions: Does not apply where the owner or a family member resides in the same residential building and shares a bathroom or kitchen with the tenant; conduct necessary to comply with program requirements related to source of income is allowed; landlords may still reject applicants for other lawful reasons.
rules.penalty: Private court action within one year of discovery for violations on or after August 1, 2019; injunction; mandatory award of three times one month's rent (charged rent if during tenancy, advertised rent if before tenancy); punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs; City enforcement under Chapter 1.
rules.quoted_span: (a) It is unlawful for any person to do any of the following acts, wholly or in part, based on a person’s source of income  (except as may be necessary to comply with any program requirements related to source of income ):
rules.interaction: Defines source of income more broadly than the California Fair Employment and Housing Act, explicitly including rental assistance and subsidies from federal, state, local, or nonprofit programs; does not limit rights under other housing discrimination laws.

notes: Division took effect 10-18-2018, but the private right of action in § 98.0806(a) only covers violations occurring on or after August 1, 2019. The quoted span normalizes PDF line breaks to single spaces. Owner-occupied shared-facility exemption has no unit-count limit stated, so owner_based_exemption_max_units is null.
